ui.label: Wait before and after each PC
ui.help: Time for the link to settle before a PC's first case and after its last. Example: 10 s.

ui.label: Measure time per direction
ui.help: How long iperf3 measures send, then receive, in each case. Example: 30 s.

ui.label: Pass threshold, wired
ui.help: A wired case passes when send and receive each reach this share of the link speed the card actually got (1000 Mbps link: 900 Mbps). Wi-Fi shows values only.

ui.label: Protocol
ui.help: TCP measures what a download gets. UDP sends at 95 % of the link speed and reports loss and jitter.

ui.label: Parallel connections
ui.help: iperf3 connections at once (-P). 1 is how one download behaves; more can fill fast links.

ui.label: Link speeds
ui.help: Every supported: each cable is measured at every speed and duplex its card supports (and the WAN-side card's, with the first cable), and each Wi-Fi band at every width cap and mode its card offers, then put back. As it is: only the link as it came up.

ui.label: Directions
ui.help: LAN→WAN: the LAN-side PC sends to the WAN-side PC (iperf3, upload). WAN→LAN: the WAN-side PC sends to the LAN-side PC (iperf3 -R, download). Both: two separate runs, LAN→WAN first, never at the same time.

ui.label: UDP rate
ui.help: UDP only: iperf3 -b at this share of the link speed the card got (1000 Mbps link, 95 %: -b 950M). TCP takes what the path gives.

ui.label: Cards to test
ui.help: Tick in Devices each card to measure: a wired card on the router LAN side, or a Wi-Fi card with the router's open Wi-Fi picked for 2.4 / 5 / 6 GHz (from that card's scan). Nothing is ticked for you.
